key: Two music teachers in the same Chennai colony
name: ch29_music_teacher_two_ways
alt: Split picture of the same middle-aged man at two music classes: on the left a teacher with a long list of crosses sends him to sit with small children and he walks out; on the right a teacher praises his ear and marks only one thing to fix, and he sits happily with a calendar of Sundays.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, the same 45-year-old man (round spectacles, cream kurta, slightly greying hair, a small cloth bag) appearing in both halves. LEFT panel: a small music room in a Chennai colony house with a woven mat on the floor and a tanpura leaning on the wall. A stern teacher in her fifties in a dark plum silk sari stands pointing at a tall checklist on a board showing three rows, each with a red cross beside a small icon of lungs, a musical note and a bent figure. Three eight-year-old children sit cross-legged on the mat holding beginner books, and the man is shown half turned away at the door, shoulders slumped, walking out. Label "START OVER" centred at the top of the left panel. RIGHT panel: another room in the same colony, a warm teacher in her sixties in a teal cotton sari sits on the mat beside the tanpura, smiling and gesturing with an open palm toward the man, who sits upright and pleased across from her. Next to them a smaller checklist shows two green ticks beside an ear icon and a note icon and only one amber circle beside the lungs icon. A wall calendar behind them has every Sunday circled in a row. Label "FIX ONE THING" centred at the top of the right panel. Soft morning light through a window in both panels; the left feels cold and heavy, the right warm and encouraging.

key: Teaching your mother to book train tickets
name: ch29_mother_train_app
alt: Split picture of a son teaching his mother a ticket app on a phone: on the left he scolds and takes the phone back; on the right he shows three steps with the first two ticked, and later she books a ticket by herself.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, showing the same living room with a cane sofa and a wall calendar. In both halves sit a mother in her late fifties (green printed cotton sari, hair in a bun, reading spectacles on her nose) and her son in his late twenties (blue T-shirt, jeans). LEFT panel: the son leans over, frowning, and pulls the phone out of her hands while waving a finger; the mother sits back with folded arms and a hurt, closed face. A small red cross badge floats above the phone. Label "ALL WRONG" centred at the top of the left panel. RIGHT panel: the mother holds the phone herself, leaning forward with interest, while the son sits beside her pointing at the screen with an encouraging smile. A large inset bubble above them shows the phone screen enlarged as three stacked steps: a small train icon with a green tick, a calendar icon with a green tick, and a third step with a person icon and a rupee coin still waiting with an amber dot. A small inset in the top right corner of the right panel shows a later moment: the mother alone at the same sofa, phone in hand, a printed ticket icon beside her and a proud smile. Label "ALMOST DONE" centred at the top of the right panel. Warm afternoon light; the left side feels tense, the right side relaxed and confident.

name: ch29_wedding_two_steps
alt: At a Kerala wedding, an aunt shows a hesitant young man just two foot steps, left and right, and points to the drummer, linking the beat to the tabla he already plays.
scene: A wide scene at a family wedding hall in Kerala at evening: strings of marigold and jasmine garlands loop across the top, a decorated stage with a banana-leaf arch at the back right, and a small open dance floor in the centre. On the left, a young man in his twenties in a white shirt and cream mundu with a gold border stands stiffly, hands half raised in protest, a little nervous smile. His cousin, a young woman in a bright coral half-sari, tugs his wrist toward the floor. Beside him his aunt in her fifties, in a cream kasavu sari with a gold border and jasmine in her hair, laughs and demonstrates by lifting one foot: on the floor in front of them two big footprint shapes are marked with arrows, one labelled with a left arrow and one with a right arrow. On the right, a drummer in a white mundu plays a drum, and a dashed curved line with small music notes runs from the drum to a small thought bubble above the young man showing a pair of tabla, to show he already knows the beat. In the background three relatives in a loose circle clap and dance, smiling. Label "JUST TWO STEPS" centred near the top, below the garlands. Warm festive lighting, golden and joyful, low stakes and everyone laughing.

key: A boy in a Pune housing society keeps taking
name: ch29_engineer_hands_boy
alt: In a housing society, neighbours frown at a boy surrounded by a taken-apart radio and watch, while a retired engineer kneels beside him with a screwdriver; a small inset shows the boy grown up at his own repair shop.
scene: A scene in the ground-floor common area of a Pune housing society, with a lift door and its button panel on the left wall and a notice board. In the centre a boy of about eleven (striped T-shirt, shorts, curious bright eyes) sits on the floor surrounded by the parts of an old wooden radio: its cover off, a speaker, screws, a coil of wire, and a wristwatch opened beside it. Behind him on the left, two neighbours stand frowning: a woman in a salwar kameez with hands on hips and a man in a vest pointing at the mess, a small red exclamation badge above them. On the right, a retired engineer in his late sixties (white hair, spectacles, half-sleeve checked shirt, grey trousers) kneels beside the boy with a friendly smile, holding out a small screwdriver and a hand-drawn diagram of the radio with dotted arrows showing where each part goes back. Label "ENGINEER'S HANDS" centred at the top. In the upper right corner, a round inset bubble with a dotted tail shows the same boy twenty years later as a man in a teal shop apron behind a counter of a small repair-and-electronics shop, with radios and phones on shelves and a soldering iron in his hand. Soft daylight from the stairwell; the mood shifts from annoyed on the left to hopeful on the right.

key: A father in Lucknow teaching his son cycling
name: ch29_cycling_records_kulfi
alt: In a colony lane, a father runs beside his son on a bicycle while chalk marks on the road show his growing records of 5, 8 and 12 metres; neighbours cheer from balconies and a kulfi waits as the reward.
scene: A wide evening scene in a Lucknow colony lane lined with two-storey houses with small balconies. The road runs left to right. On the left, the father in his late thirties (white kurta, grey trousers, sandals) jogs a few steps behind, one hand just let go of the seat, smiling and cheering. In the middle, his eight-year-old son rides a small red bicycle with a wobble, tongue out in concentration, feet on the pedals. Along the road three chalk lines are drawn across the tarmac with chalk numbers beside them: "5 m" near the start, "8 m" further on, and "12 m" ahead of the boy's front wheel, with a dashed arrow from the bicycle showing it is about to pass the newest line. Above, on two balconies, neighbours lean over the railing clapping: an elderly woman in a sari and a young man in a T-shirt raising both arms. On the right edge, a kulfi seller's small cart with a red cloth cover and a kulfi on a stick held up on display, waiting as the reward. Label "NEW RECORD" centred near the top above the lane. Warm orange sunset light, long soft shadows, a happy and proud mood that shows progress being measured and celebrated each evening.

key: A boy in a Bihar village school sits on the back
name: ch29_back_bench_change
alt: In a village classroom, a new teacher asks a boy on the back bench to work out the change from a 500 rupee note; he answers correctly, classmates clap, and a dotted arrow shows him moving toward the front.
scene: A view of a simple village school classroom in Bihar with whitewashed walls, a window with iron bars and a dark green blackboard at the front left. Wooden benches run in rows toward the back right. At the front, a young new teacher in her twenties in a mustard cotton sari stands beside the blackboard, holding up a pink 500-rupee note in one hand and smiling encouragingly. On the blackboard is a simple sum with the note and a few coins drawn in chalk. At the back right, on the last bench, a thin boy of about twelve in a white school shirt and navy shorts stands up confidently with fingers raised as if counting, a speech bubble near him showing a small pile of notes and a green tick. Two or three classmates on the middle benches turn around and clap, smiling. The last bench has a faded label "BACK BENCH" on the floor beneath it, and a curved dotted arrow runs from the boy toward an empty spot on the front bench, showing him moving closer to the board. A small inset in the top right corner shows a thought of his uncle's kirana shop counter with a cash box and coins, where he learned to count money. The teacher's note shows "500". Bright morning light through the window, hopeful and warm.

key: A good driving instructor in a Delhi learner
name: ch29_clutch_one_thing
alt: Split picture inside a learner car stalled on a slope: on the left a sighing instructor says the student will never learn; on the right an instructor praises the steady steering and practises only the clutch in an empty lot.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, each half showing a small white learner car with a red L sign on its roof. LEFT panel: the car is stuck on a short slope in a Delhi street, a small puff of smoke from the bonnet and a stall icon, a red cross badge above it. Through the side window we see the student, a young woman in her early twenties in a lilac kurta, gripping the wheel and looking upset, and the instructor, a man in his forties in a grey safari shirt, slumped back with his hand on his forehead, sighing. Label "NEVER" centred at the top of the left panel. RIGHT panel: the same car in a wide empty parking lot with a few painted lines, on level ground. The instructor, now a calm older man in a teal shirt, sits relaxed, pointing at the floor pedals with an encouraging smile while the student smiles with focus. A large round inset bubble shows the clutch pedal with a slow upward arrow and a little wavy shiver line, then an arrow to the accelerator pedal. Beside the car a tally of ten small marks, most of them ticked green, shows the repeated practice, and a green tick on the steering wheel shows the part already done well. Label "JUST ONE THING" centred at the top of the right panel. Clear daylight; the left tense and grey, the right sunny and calm.
